findings.where: <repo>/docs/spec/ane-port-limits-h17.html L98-99 (callout 'The model in one paragraph')
findings.claim: A program executes iff its live ports fit in 127 and its declared ports fit in 255.
findings.reality: The 255 bound applies to declared ports only at validate and compile. The run path prunes dead inputs first, so a file with declared ports above 255 still executes. The page says this itself at L133-136, and the writeup says the 255 applies to live ports on the run path (md L129-131).
findings.evidence: ane-port-limits-h17.spec L128-135: gen_mix_ports 255 1 is rejected by validate (rc 1, MaxLiveInLiveOutExceeded) and runs (rc 0, step 0) on the run path. md L129-131.
findings.fix: State two conditions: execution needs live_in + n_states + unique_out + n_exposed_states <= 127; validate and compile additionally need declared_in + n_states + out + n_exposed_states <= 255.

findings.where: <repo>/docs/spec/ane-port-limits-h17.html L251 (row [1,300,1,31]) and L254 (row [1,86,1,80])
findings.claim: rows <= 256 is sufficient, not necessary.
findings.reality: Sufficiency holds only when d3 <= 32. The page's own row [1,86,1,80] has 86 rows (<= 256) and fails with status=0x1d. The spec header says rows <= 256 is SUFFICIENT when d3 <= 32 (spec L15), and md L478 has the same qualifier.
findings.evidence: ane-port-limits-h17.spec L516-518 (gen_states_nd 1 1 86 1 80 gives status=0x1d); spec L15.
findings.fix: Write: rows <= 256 is sufficient when d3 <= 32.

findings.where: <repo>/docs/spec/ane-port-limits-h17.html L102-103 (callout), L211 (8 B trailer member), L222-224 (special slot words)
findings.claim: Every task block ends with a flat trailer of 12-byte buffer bindings whose slot word is a BAR id.
findings.reality: The trailer also holds three 8-byte records (0x1340, 0x1341, 0x1440), which the page's own section 4 diagram shows at L211. Slot words below 0x2300 are special, not BAR ids, as the page's own note at L222-224 and md L271-276 say. The word 'every' is not asserted: spec L321-322 asserts only the 1x full-trailer line, not the 53x and 53x counts, and decode_block_trailers.py trailer() and main loop accept an empty trailer.
findings.evidence: md L294-296 (trailer = [9344 12B][934a 12B]* [9442 12B][1340 8B][1341 8B][1440 8B], any subset); scripts/decode_block_trailers.py trailer() and main loop (no empty-trailer check); spec L321-322.
findings.fix: Describe the flat trailer as 12-byte bindings followed by 8-byte records, any subset; slot word is a BAR ordinal or a special word below 0x2300.

findings.where: <repo>/docs/spec/ane-port-limits-h17.html L227-229 (section 5 tag formula)
findings.claim: tag = 0x9261 + 0x100·[dim1 != 1] + 0x004·[dim0 != 1] − 0x001·[dim1 = 16], applied to a state.

findings.fix: Name the role: '[dim0 field present]', which applies to the state-out record only; the update-row record has no dim0 field.

findings.where: ane-port-limits-h17.md §6 'Word-level fields' table (flag word, slice rows); ane-port-limits-h17.html §5 table rows 'flag word' and 'slice'; contradicts the header comment of scripts/decode_copy_words.py
findings.claim: flag word = 0x8000 | 0x08·[dim1≠1] | 0x20·[dim0≠1]; slice = pitch·dim1 (present when dim0≠1 and dim1≠1). Labeled 'established', no dim2 domain given, and the page says every number is spec-asserted.
findings.reality: Both laws hold only at dim2 = 1 with (dim0, dim1) ≠ (1, 1). (a) dim2 > 1: flag word gains 0x04 (0x802c, not 0x8028) and the slice word changes. +0x32 becomes pitch·d2, and a new word at +0x36 holds pitch·d1·d2. So slice = pitch·dim1 is wrong there. (b) dim0 = dim1 = 1 (d2 = 1): flag word is 0x0000 and no pitch or slice words exist. The pitch word at +0x2e = 64·⌈d3/32⌉ does hold at d2 = 2, 3, 5, but decode_copy_words.py prints pitch='-' for d2 ≠ 1, so 'padded = rows·pitch' (§7) for d2 > 1 cannot be read from the tool. The decoder's own header documents both exceptions ('| 0x04 when dim2 > 1; 0x0000 when dim0 == dim1 == 1'), so tool and writeup disagree. d2 > 1 is the KV layout [2L,kvh,S,hd] that §9 rule 4 cites.
findings.evidence: gen_states_nd.py 1 4 7 3 33 1 1 direct (h17), read at tag+0x28/+0x2e/+0x32/+0x36 of the first 0x9365 record: flagw=0x802c, pitch=128, +0x32=384 (=128·3), +0x36=2688 (=128·3·7). The law predicts slice=896 and flagw=0x8028. Same pattern at [4,7,3,96] (576/4032), [4,3,5,65] (960/2880), [4,7,2,31] (128/896), each twice. gen_states_nd.py 1 4 5 3 33: decode_copy_words.py gives flagw=802c pitch=- slice=-. gen_states_nd.py 1 1 1 1 33 (and gen_states_nd.py 2 1 1 1 33 with --last): flagw=0000 pitch=- slice=-. gen_states_nd.py 1 1 1 3 33: flagw=8004. Raw dump of [4,5,3,33] vs [4,5,1,33] in WD/rec.py output.
findings.fix: State the domain: flag word = 0x8000|0x08[d1≠1]|0x20[d0≠1]|0x04[d2>1], and 0 when d0=d1=d2=1. State slice = pitch·dim1 for d2 = 1, and that at d2 > 1 the words are pitch·d2 and pitch·d1·d2. State that pitch holds at d2 > 1 but the decoder does not print it. Apply the same fix to the HTML rows.

findings.where: ane-port-limits-h17.md §6 'SHORT word map ... 1M is ⌈d3/8⌉ MiB' and 'Row width' bullets; ane-port-limits-h17.html §5 row 'row width: rowbits = 16·dim1·⌈d3/8⌉' (untagged, so claimed spec-asserted)
findings.claim: The first SHORT word is ⌈d3/8⌉ MiB, and rowbits = 16·dim1·⌈d3/8⌉. The md calls the 1M word 'established' with no domain, and hedges rowbits only as 'up to a dim1-dependent saturation (tentative)'. The HTML gives the rowbits formula with no qualifier.
findings.reality: Both laws hold for d3 ≤ 128 at every dim1 tried (2 to 300). Beyond that they break. The first word saturates: 32 MiB (0x02000000) for dim1 = 2 at every d3 from 257 to 4097. At dim1 ≥ 8 it caps at 16 MiB (0x01000000) from d3 = 129. At dim1 = 8 the pattern is non-monotone: d3 = 129, 160, 192 give 16 MiB, but 224 gives 28 and 255 gives 32. rowbits caps the same way. Separately, rowbits is a u16 that wraps mod 2^16 rather than saturating. The md's word 'saturation' is imprecise. The spec's 'RB' label is self-referential (it compares to the decoder-read rowbits), so no spec line asserts 16·dim1·⌈d3/8⌉ for d3 > 8.
findings.fix: Add the domain (d3 ≤ 128) to the 1M law, or state the cap (16 MiB for dim1 ≥ 8, 32 MiB for dim1 = 2 and 4). Say that rowbits is u16-wrapped and capped. Tag the HTML 'row width' row tentative/runner.

findings.where: ane-port-limits-h17.md §6 'SHORT word map: 1M, RB, RB, RB | RB' and 'In both layouts exactly four words equal rowbits << 16'; HTML §5 'row width' row ('four words = rowbits << 16, SHORT: 1M, RB, RB, RB | RB')
findings.claim: The SHORT map is 1M,RB,RB,RB|RB, and exactly four words equal rowbits<<16 in both layouts. The 'Direct' qualifier appears only on the LONG bullet.
findings.reality: True only for a directly-used plain-input update source. For a computed update source (the generator default 'add' mode), SHORT records carry extra low bits. The first word is 1M|0x10 and the last is RB|0x40, so only three words equal RB. The computed LONG form 803e/0142 also differs from the stated maps.
findings.evidence: gen_states_nd.py 1 4 4 1 D3 1 3 add, decode_copy_words.py: D3=1 gives form=803c/0142 map=0x00100010,RB,RB,RB|0x00400040; D3=9 gives 0x00200010,RB,RB,RB|0x00800040; D3=33 gives 0x00500010,RB,RB,RB|0x01400040 (twice each). The same shapes with 'direct' give 1M / 0x00200000 / 0x00500000, RB,RB,RB|RB. gen_states_nd.py 1 4 4 1 1 2 2 add gives form=803e/0142 map=0x00800040,1M,RB,RB,RB|0x00c00000, and (3,2) gives 0x00900010,1M,RB,RB,RB|0x00d00040. The 803e/0142-needs-≥2-in-≥2-out claim itself held at (2,2),(3,2),(2,5),(4,4) and failed to appear at (1,x),(x,1).
findings.fix: Mark both maps and the 'four words' sentence as direct-source only, and note the computed-source SHORT map (1M|0x10 … RB|0x40) and LONG map. Or drop the 'in both layouts' wording.

findings.where: ane-port-limits-h17.md §5 'u32 tail ... is the next block's pre-frame window ... [1][(stride class+1)<<16|1][0x10001][d3][d2][d1]. It is independent of N and dim0, and identical on both arches'
findings.claim: The pre-frame window of the block after the first 0x9344 block is the 6-word copy-header mirror, with the stated word values and no stated domain.
findings.reality: The law held at dim1 in {1,2,3,5,9,33,64}, d3=3, N in {1,2,3,7,53}, dim0 in {1,4,8}, on h17 and h16g, twice each. It fails at three edges. (1) dim1 = 16: the window has only 5 words, '1,50001,8001,3,1', with the d1 word absent and the third word 0x8001. This is the same elision as tag 0x9360. The md gives only the 0x10001 form, and the 0x8001 variant appears only in the task text, not the md. (2) When the next block is a compute block rather than a copy record, the second word is 1, not (class+1)<<16|1: window '1,1,10001,d3,d2,d1', frame 0x9541 or 0x9d41. This affects 4 of the 6 varied programs run: no-input, conv=1, lut=sigmoid, packed (gen_states 0 5 51), and also a plain 'add' with 2 in 2 out. (3) 'stride class' is not a function of dim1 alone: it follows the stride word, which gains bits at d2 > 1 or d3 ≥ 129. The spec asserts only dim1 = 4 and 9.

findings.where: ane-port-limits-h17.md §5 'Nothing is embedded inside 0x9344 or 0x9361. No trailer tag occurs outside a trailer.' and decode_block_trailers.py chain_ok; also count_desc_records.py as the basis of the '0x9344 = K + max(1, min(in,out))' count law
findings.claim: No trailer tag value occurs outside a trailer, so chain_ok=1 holds for all valid programs, and 0x9344 counts are raw record counts.
findings.reality: A state dimension equal to a tag value appears as a 2-byte-aligned u16 in the copy-record header. The decoder's 'stray tag' check then reports chain_ok=0 (exit 1) although idx chain, end alignment and trailer parsing are all valid. The raw-u16 scan in count_desc_records.py also inflates counts. This is an edge case (huge or specially chosen dims), but the sentence is false as written.
findings.evidence: gen_states_nd.py 2 4 4 1 4928 1 1 direct gives blocks=5 chain_ok=0. Also d3=4929 (0x1341), d3=5184 (0x1440) and [4,4928,1,32]; d3=4960 gives chain_ok=1. A custom stray scan shows u32 0x1340 at block+0x28 and +0x38, with chain(idx+end)=True. gen_states_nd.py 1 4 4 1 37700 1 1 direct (37700 = 0x9344): count_desc_records.py prints '0x9344 records: 8' while the trailers contain 2 (d3=4096 gives 2).
findings.fix: Say the invariant holds for dims that do not collide with tag values, or make the decoder test the stray tags by parsed field positions. Note that the count law was measured with a raw u16 scan.

findings.where: ane-port-limits-h17.md §6 '(2 MiB at d3 = 9, 5 MiB at d3 = 33; asserted)'; ane-port-limits-h17.html §6 state table 'pitch' column (opening claim: every number is spec-asserted unless tagged runner)
findings.claim: 2 MiB at d3 = 9 is spec-asserted. The pitch values in the page's state table are spec-asserted.
findings.reality: The values are correct. The label 'asserted' is not supported for them. The spec asserts the first word only at d3 = 1 ('1M') and d3 = 33 (0x00500000). Nothing asserts d3 = 9 (the '2097152' at spec line 405 is region at dim1 = 2, not the first word). The spec asserts pitch only at (d3=1, dim1=2) and (d3=33, dim1=4). The table's pitch values 64 at d3 = 31 and 32 and 192 at d3 = 80 are closed-form values with no spec line. Reproducing the d0 = 1 rows' pitch needs 'decode_copy_words.py --last'. The default invocation prints nothing for those states because they have no dim0 flag, and neither document says so.
